rounds.text: Jyoti Resins and Adhesives Ltd presents a compelling value opportunity, trading at an attractive P/E ratio of 16.7x alongside a market capitalization of ₹ 1,097 Cr [E1, E3]. The business demonstrates elite capital efficiency, boasting a robust ROCE of 36.5% and an ROE of 27.0%, backed by a stellar 10-year median ROE of 37% [E12, E13, E26]. Long-term compounding remains exceptional, evidenced by 10-year and 5-year compounded sales growth of 21% and 25%, alongside extraordinary profit growth of 78% and 44% over the same periods [E14, E15, E18, E19]. Furthermore, the company is almost debt-free with zero borrowings, generating healthy operating and free cash flows of ₹ 48 Cr and ₹ 44 Cr respectively as of March 2026 [E35, E36, E56]. Promoter confidence is clearly expanding, with insider holdings increasing by 3.92 percentage points from March 2024 to 54.75% in October 2026 [E40]. Conceded: operating margins have faced recent pressure with a TTM decrease to 23% and working capital days have risen to 83.0 days [E30, E60]. Nevertheless, fundamentals continue to significantly outpace share price performance, leaving the stock well-positioned for re-rating [E53].

Despite headline growth metrics, Jyoti Resins and Adhesives Ltd carries acute operational and valuation vulnerabilities that the headline figures obscure. Most alarmingly, the company suffers from severely bloated receivables, boasting high debtors of 185 days alongside a doubling of working capital days from 41.4 days to 83.0 days [E59, E60]. This liquidity strain coincides with deteriorating profitability trends, as compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months has turned negative at -10% [E21], and the operating margin has contracted by 10 percentage points from three years earlier down to 23% in the TTM [E30]. Furthermore, the yearly operating-margin trend reads as decreasing over the last four years [E32], while quarterly margins have shown inconsistency [E33]. Valuation comparisons also reveal stark disconnects against sector benchmarks; specifically, the price-to-book ratio sits at 3.59x compared to a sector benchmark of just 1.7x, and key profitability metrics such as ROA (0.07%), ROE (0.07%), and ROCE (0.22%) severely underperform sector benchmarks of 5.67%, 9.33%, and 11.09% respectively [E7, E8, E9, E10]. Conceded: the company maintains a debt-free status [E37], strong historical multi-year sales and profit growth [E14, E15, E18, E19], and a high ROCE in filed statements [E12].

The bear flags high debtors of 185 days and rising working capital days [E59, E60], but glosses over the robust ₹ 48 Cr in operating cash flow and ₹ 44 Cr in free cash flow generated as of March 2026 [E35, E36]. Conceded: TTM compounded profit growth is -10% [E21], but this short-term dip contrasts sharply with exceptional multi-year compounding, including 78% 10-year and 44% 5-year profit growth [E18, E19]. While the bear highlights P/B against an external data provider's sector benchmark [E7], it ignores the company's verified return metrics from filed statements, such as a stellar 36.5% ROCE and 27.0% ROE [E12, E13]. Furthermore, the alarm over decreasing yearly operating margins [E32] misses that the business maintains an elite debt-free balance sheet with 0.00x debt to equity and flat zero borrowings [E37, E38]. Lastly, the market price is heavily discounted against a rigorous DCF intrinsic value calculation, leaving a substantial 59.2% margin of safety while pricing in only 5.7% earnings growth [E44, E45, E46].

Conceded: the company generated Rs 48 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs 44 Cr in free cash flow as of March 2026 [E35, E36], but that cash generation sits alongside severe working capital deterioration where debtors stretch to 185 days and working capital days nearly double from 41.4 to 83.0 days [E59, E60]. While the bull points to historical multi-year compounding like 78% 10-year and 44% 5-year profit growth [E18, E19], this ignores the immediate reality that TTM compounded profit growth has contracted by -10% [E21] and 3-year share price growth has fallen -18% [E24]. Conceded: the company reports a 36.5% ROCE and 27.0% ROE [E12, E13], yet third-party data provider key-ratios place its ROA at a meager 0.07%, ROE at 0.07%, and ROCE at 0.22% against much higher sector benchmarks [E8, E9, E10]. Dismissing the operating-margin trend ignores that yearly operating margins have been steadily decreasing over the last four years [E32], dropping by 10 percentage points in TTM and 5 percentage points in the Sep 2026 quarter [E30, E31]. Finally, leaning on a theoretical reverse DCF to downplay earnings growth requirements [E46] fails to justify why the stock's 1-year performance has plummeted by -25% [E25] while institutional money flows remain strictly neutral [E43].
